dod_intent_evidence: Real but exclusively SBIR-shaped: an Air Force 2022 Phase II ($1,250,000) for the 'NV-Biosensor platform for quantum-based single molecule detection', and a LinkedIn about line — 'developing a quantum sensor for disease detection under contracts with the U.S. Air Force and National Cancer Institute'. No product, program, or non-SBIR defense customer appears anywhere.
score_evidence: SBIR.gov firm record (news section): 'Year of first award: 2005 | 6 Phase I Awards | 4 Phase II Awards | 66.67% Conversion Rate | $1,657,190 Phase I Dollars | $3,941,351 Phase II Dollars | $5,598,541 Total' with 'Number of Employees: 4' → twenty-one years and $5.6M of federal R&D at four people; the award stream is the business model

The awards span unrelated agencies and topics — USAF quantum biosensing, NIH 'POSTURE ANALYSIS THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING (PATHML)' Phase I (HHS/NIH, $354,99x, 2023) — the pattern of a shop that writes to whatever topic is open rather than fielding one capability

'The deliverables for this project include results and reports on the design of the NV-Biosensor, a prototype point of care device for the NV-Biosensor, and a demonstration of the technology to the Air Force.' (sbir_abstract) → the contract's own end state is a report, a prototype, and a demo

Commercial product motion has been spun out rather than scaled: 'Columbus Nanoworks Now Offers Its Life Sciences and Biomedical Products Through Its Subsidiary' pointing to cymaris.com — the sellable thing is nanodiamond reagents for other people's research, not a fielded system

Own-language word count is ~713 (under the 1000 threshold) and the entire non-SBIR site copy is materials-science description of fluorescent diamonds — there is no product, roadmap, customer, or deployment surface to engage
what_they_do: Four-person Columbus, Ohio lab that makes fluorescent nanodiamonds and is developing an NV-center quantum biosensor to detect biomarkers such as microRNA and cortisol at single-molecule sensitivity, funded by Air Force and NIH SBIRs since 2005.
